items.title: NEURODIVERSITY, INCLUSION AND INTERGENERATIONAL EDUCATION: POSSIBLE CONVERGENCES IN LIGHT OF LEARNING THEORIES
items.summary: This article investigates the interfaces between neurodiversity, inclusive pedagogical practices, and intergenerational education, based on theories of human learning. The central research question is: how can the principles of learning theories—behaviorism, cognitivism, sociointeractionism, and humanism—support pedagogical practices that integrate inclusion and intergenerationality in contexts of neurodiversity? items.summary: Post-stroke spasticity is a common and clinically consequential manifestation of the upper motor neuron syndrome, yet its mechanisms are incompletely explained by stretch reflex hyperexcitability alone. Thus, to explore possible neural bases for translation asymmetry, there is a distinct need to examine word translations by intermediate L2 learners. items.title: Magnetogenetics: Tools for Noninvasive Neuromodulation with Cellular Resolution
items.summary: Magnetogenetics is emerging as a promising tool to control neuronal activity and overcome the limitations of chemogenetics and optogenetics. While chemogenetics is restricted in temporal resolution, optogenetics is invasive and limited in penetration depth. Magnetogenetics addresses these challenges by offering a noninvasive approach that enables wireless and on-demand control of neuronal activity. items.title: Effects of neural aging on speech perception in bilinguals vs. monolinguals
items.summary: This study examined the effects of aging and bilingualism on neural speech perception in Spanish-English (SE) bilinguals and American English (AE) monolinguals. As the population of bilingual older adults continues to grow, understanding how bilingual experience influences auditory processing across the lifespan has important theoretical and clinical implications. items.title: Ketogenic diet and Parkinson’s disease
items.summary: Parkinson’s disease (PD), a common degenerative disorder in middle-aged and elderly individuals, has an unclear etiology and pathogenesis, and there is currently no cure. In recent years, the ketogenic diet (KD), a dietary regimen characterized by high-fat, extremely low carbohydrates, and moderate protein intake, has shown promise in the treatment of PD. items.summary: Variations in neural circuitry, inherited or acquired, may underlie important individual differences in thought, feeling, and action patterns. items.title: Beyond Greed: A Systems Perspective on Human Desire, Exploitation, and Cooperative Incentive Design
items.summary: Abstract Why does exploitation persist across civilizations despite the emergence of legal systems, ethical norms, and democratic institutions? Conventional explanations often attribute exploitation to individual moral failure, greed, or deficiencies in character. While these perspectives capture important aspects of human behavior, they provide only a partial account of why exploitative patterns repeatedly emerge across widely different historical, political, and economic contexts. items.title: Mental Health Disorders, Suicide Attempts, Substance Use, and Substance Use Disorders in Adults with Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders: A Gender-Separated Study
items.summary: Abstract Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD) are a group of neurodevelopmental disorders caused by alcohol exposure during pregnancy. FASD is associated with various neurocognitive disorders over the entire lifespan. Comorbid mental health disorders seem to be highly prevalent. Suicide attempts and substance use as well as substance use disorders are also associated with FASD in adults. However, previous studies report small or very selective samples. items.summary: Background/Objectives: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a chronic pain condition characterized by widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and psychosocial challenges. items.title: Hippocampal–Cortical Circuits and Memory
items.summary: This review examines how distributed neural circuits involving the hippocampus, entorhinal cortex, and neocortex collectively support learning and memory functions. The hippocampus and entorhinal cortex are densely and bidirectionally connected, forming a core circuit that supports the formation of episodic memories as well as spatial learning and navigation.
